claims.claim: A sensitive call from a task Solix launched is held until a human answers.
The gate works on a non-default port.
The command denylist refuses at every level, including `observe`, for everything Solix launches.
The floor applies even when the session row cannot be found.
An unreachable gate denies rather than waving the command through.
Stopping Solix refuses what it is holding and exits, rather than hanging.
`solix run` adds a side channel, **not** governance.
A verified task's acceptance criteria cannot be changed afterwards, and a task cannot be marked done without running. "Verified against its acceptance criteria" means what it says.
claims.publishedIn: site ("verified, not assumed"), Maestro section, brief

claims.claim: Every cost and token figure is the sum of the transcript, counted once — it does not grow when Solix restarts.
claims.publishedIn: site ("watch the money", "every number is live and local"), Mission Control, `solix gain`, `solix ledger`

claims.claim: Solix never chooses a network destination. Every outbound request goes somewhere the user configured. Nothing is collected and nothing is sent on its own.
Only a loopback origin can drive the control plane.
A galaxy manifest URL cannot be turned into a probe of the local network.
You hear about a held decision after you have walked away.
`solix uninstall` leaves your Claude config exactly as it found it.
Install refuses to write a `settings.json` it could not read.
Installing a team twice does not create its routines twice.
`solix demo` seeds a real galaxy into its own sandbox database and cleans up after itself — and when a seed write is rejected it says how many, instead of printing a summary over them.
Every `solix doctor` check can both pass and fail, looks where Solix actually is, and degrades to "unknown" rather than to a verdict when it cannot reach the server.
claims.publishedIn: brief, install guide, three error messages
